questions.q: Antonio Toledo is credited with the design of the Manila City Hall. What is the most famous, albeit controversial, architectural characteristic of this building's floor plan?
o: It is shaped like a perfect star
It is a perfect replica of the U.S. Capitol
It resembles a casket or coffin from an aerial view
questions.n: The unique hexagonal tower and tapering wings create an unintended shape that is frequently compared to a casket.

questions.q: Toledo worked on the Legislative Building, which was originally intended to be the National Library. What is the current function of this grand neoclassical structure?
o: The National Museum of Natural History
The National Museum of Fine Arts
The Supreme Court of the Philippines
questions.n: The former Legislative Building, co-designed with Juan Arellano, now houses the nation's premier art collection.

questions.q: Which major university campus in Manila features several buildings designed by Toledo, following the strict neoclassical style favored by the Bureau of Public Works?
questions.n: Toledo designed several buildings for the UP campus in Ermita, including the original College of Medicine structures.

questions.q: The Leyte Provincial Capitol in Tacloban is one of Toledo's most famous regional works. Why is this building historically significant beyond its architecture?
o: It served as the temporary seat of the Commonwealth Government in 1944
It was the site of the signing of the Treaty of Manila
It was the first building in the Philippines to use steel
It was designed to be earthquake-proof using bamboo
questions.n: During the liberation of the Philippines, President Sergio Osmeña used this capitol as the government headquarters.

questions.q: Antonio Toledo was known for his mastery of the 'Classical Orders.' Which of these features would you most likely find on a Toledo-designed government facade?
o: Ionic or Corinthian columns with a formal pediment
Ornate Baroque carvings of tropical fruits
questions.n: These are the fundamental elements of the Neoclassical style that Toledo mastered throughout his career.

questions.q: Antonio Toledo was known for his mastery of Neoclassicism. Which of these buildings is a prime example of his work for the Department of Agriculture and Commerce, now part of the National Museum complex?
o: The National Library of the Philippines
questions.n: Toledo designed this building, originally the Agriculture and Commerce Building, featuring a grand neoclassical facade that mirrors its twin across the circle.

questions.q: Carlos Barretto was the first Filipino to graduate with an architecture degree from abroad. In which American city did he complete his studies at the Drexel Institute?
questions.n: The Drexel Institute of Art, Science, and Industry, where Barretto graduated in 1908, is located in Philadelphia.

questions.q: Which specific architectural 'order' did Antonio Toledo use for the massive columns of the Legislative Building (now National Museum of Fine Arts)?
questions.n: The Corinthian order, with its acanthus leaf capitals, was chosen to convey the highest level of dignity and grandeur for the seat of the legislature.

questions.q: Carlos Barretto's career was largely spent in the Bureau of Public Works. What was his official professional registration number?
questions.n: As one of the pioneers, Barretto was the second architect to be officially registered in the Philippines.

questions.q: Toledo's Manila City Hall is often criticized for its 'coffin' shape. Architecturally, what was the primary reason for the building's asymmetrical and tapering wings?
o: To create a wind tunnel for cooling
To symbolize the end of Spanish rule
To follow the irregular shape of the lot
questions.n: The building was designed to maximize the available land area of the trapezoidal lot provided by the city.

questions.q: Both Toledo and Barretto worked under the supervision of which famous American consulting architect who drafted the plans for Manila and Baguio?
questions.n: Parsons was the Consulting Architect for the Philippine government who mentored the first generation of Filipino architects.

questions.q: True or False: Carlos Barretto was the architect responsible for the final design of the Manila Central Post Office.
questions.n: Juan Arellano is the lead architect most associated with the Post Office, though Barretto was a contemporary in the same office.

questions.q: In his later career, Antonio Toledo served as the Dean of the College of Architecture for which university?
o: Manila Council of the United Architects
questions.n: Toledo served as the head of the architecture department at Adamson, helping to train the next generation of builders.
